# Executor Completion Service

When independent tasks finish at different times, collecting their futures in
submission order can leave a caller waiting for an earlier task even though a
later result is ready. `ExecutorCompletionService` lets the caller collect
completed tasks as they become available.

## Learning objectives

By the end of this example, attendees can:

- submit independent tasks and collect completed futures with `take()`;
- retrieve results and handle task failures using `Future.get()`;
- distinguish completion order from submission order and explain the relevant
  visibility guarantee; and
- describe why the executor still needs lifecycle management.

## Prerequisite

Install
[Oracle Java 8](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java8) or
newer and make it available to `java` and `javac`. Familiarity with
[Future Task](../future-task/README.md) and the
[Executor Framework](../executor-framework/README.md) is useful.

## The program to inspect

The program submits three tasks to a completion service backed by a fixed thread
pool. The first task sleeps for 500 milliseconds to make it more likely that the
other tasks complete first; one of those tasks fails. This delay does not
guarantee an order. The caller uses `take()` once per submitted task: each call
removes the next completed future, waiting if none is available. Calling `get()`
on that future retrieves the value or reports the task’s failure through
`ExecutionException`; a failed task is still a completion.

Compare this with calling `get()` on the returned futures in submission order: a
slow first task could delay handling a later completed task. Completion order is
not necessarily submission order, but scheduling determines this run’s order; it
may happen to match. `poll()` provides a non-blocking alternative, and its timed
overload waits up to a specified duration.

The completion service does not shut down its executor. The example requests
shutdown in `finally` and waits up to five seconds for termination; interruption
while collecting results is propagated with interrupt status restored. A timeout
does not itself force uncooperative tasks to stop.

```java
package demo;

import java.util.concurrent.*;

import static demo.utils.Logs.log;
import static demo.utils.Logs.logHeaderAndJavaVersion;

public final class Main {

    public static void main(final String[] args) throws InterruptedException {
        logHeaderAndJavaVersion("Executor Completion Service");

        final ExecutorService executor = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(3);
        final CompletionService<String> completed = new ExecutorCompletionService<>(executor);

        try {
            log("Submitting: first, second, third");
            completed.submit(() -> {
                TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS.sleep(500);
                return "first: result";
            });
            completed.submit(() -> {throw new IllegalStateException("second: failed");});
            completed.submit(() -> "third: result");

            for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
                final Future<String> future = completed.take();
                try {
                    log("Completed: " + future.get());
                } catch (final ExecutionException e) {
                    log("Completed with failure: " + e.getCause());
                }
            }
        } finally {
            executor.shutdownNow();
            if (!executor.awaitTermination(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS)) {
                log("Executor did not terminate within five seconds");
            }
        }
    }
}
```

The `CompletionService` contract establishes that actions before submission
happen-before task actions, which happen-before actions following the successful
return of the corresponding `take()`. The `Future` contract also specifies the
memory-consistency effect of `get()`. These guarantees do not establish an order
between independent tasks or make arbitrary shared updates atomic.

## Guided walkthrough

Run the following command from `examples/`. Compare the submission line with the
completion lines and find the failed task. Repeat the command: the order may
change, but a particular ordering is not guaranteed.

1. Run the example using the
   [Maven `exec` plugin](https://www.mojohaus.org/exec-maven-plugin/).

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean compile exec:exec
   ```

   One possible run; task and log ordering will vary.

   ```
   ...
   [12:34:56.789] [                                             Thread[main,5,main]] Executor Completion Service
   [12:34:56.791] [                                             Thread[main,5,main]] Using Java 1.8.0_511
   [12:34:56.792] [                                             Thread[main,5,main]] Submitting: first, second, third
   [12:34:56.793] [                                             Thread[main,5,main]] Completed with failure: java.lang.IllegalStateException: second: failed
   [12:34:56.793] [                                             Thread[main,5,main]] Completed: third: result
   [12:34:57.293] [                                             Thread[main,5,main]] Completed: first: result
   ...
   ```

2. Build the application and create the JAR file.

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean package
   ```

   (*Optional*) List the created JAR file.

   ```shell
   tree --dirsfirst --sort=name './target/libs'
   ```

   The application JAR file

   ```
   ./target/libs
   └── executor-completion-service-1.0.0.jar

   1 directory, 1 file
   ```

   Run the application.

   ```shell
   java \
     -classpath './target/libs/*' \
     demo.Main
   ```

   One possible run; task and log ordering will vary.

   ```
   [12:35:00.533] [                                             Thread[main,5,main]] Executor Completion Service
   [12:35:00.536] [                                             Thread[main,5,main]] Using Java 1.8.0_511
   [12:35:00.537] [                                             Thread[main,5,main]] Submitting: first, second, third
   [12:35:00.538] [                                             Thread[main,5,main]] Completed with failure: java.lang.IllegalStateException: second: failed
   [12:35:00.538] [                                             Thread[main,5,main]] Completed: third: result
   [12:35:01.038] [                                             Thread[main,5,main]] Completed: first: result
   ```
